{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Lisette G. de Pillis''' is an American mathematician at [[Harvey Mudd College]] and holds the Norman F. Sprague, Jr. Professorship of Life Sciences at Harvey Mudd.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.math.hmc.edu/people/faculty/|title=Mathematics Faculty at HMC|accessdate=2015-09-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606213225/https://www.math.hmc.edu/people/faculty/|archive-date=2017-06-06|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She chaired the Department of Mathematics in 2008-2009 and again from 2014 to 2019. She directed the Harvey Mudd College Global Clinic program from 2009 to 2014.  She is also the co-director of the Harvey Mudd College Center for Quantitative Life Sciences.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.math.hmc.edu/~depillis/KECK_QLS/index1.html|title=The Harvey Mudd College Center for Quantitative Life Sciences|accessdate=2015-09-04}}.</ref>

==Education==
De Pillis earned her Ph.D. in 1993 from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] under the supervision of [[Heinz-Otto Kreiss]]. Her dissertation was ''Far Field Behavior of Slightly Compressible Flows''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=40039}}</ref>

==Research==
Her early research concerned [[computational fluid dynamics]]. In around 2000, she became interested in [[cancer immunology]], and began doing research on [[population model]]s and [[Cellular automaton|cellular automata]] models featuring cells of three types: normal cells, cancer cells, and immune cells. By augmenting the model to include cancer treatments and applying [[control theory]], she was able to devise techniques that could lead to more effective personalized treatments for cancer.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.siam.org/news/news.php?id=1638|title=Mathematics Meets Oncology and Immunology|journal=[[SIAM News]]|date=October 18, 2009|first=Michelle|last=Sipics}}.</ref> Her continuing research has produced mathematical models of newly developing immunotherapies, combination therapies, and the emergence of autoimmune diseases.

==Recognition==
The [[Argonne National Laboratory]] named her their [[Maria Goeppert-Mayer]] Argonne Distinguished Scholar for 1999–2000.<ref>{{citation|url=http://ccms.claremont.edu/content/Lisette-dePillis-named-GoeppertMayer-Argonne-Distinguished-Scholar|title=Professor Lisette de Pillis (HMC) named Goeppert-Mayer Argonne Distinguished Scholar|date=April 1999|accessdate=2015-09-04}}.</ref>
In 2016 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-16}}.</ref>  In 2017 she was a [https://www.hersnetwork.org/programs/hers-institute/ HERS-CBL Clare Boothe Luce] Leadership in STEM Scholar. In 2019 she was awarded the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA Southern California-Nevada Section]] [http://sections.maa.org/socalnv/ Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics.] In 2020 she was made the [https://about.illinoisstate.edu/iba/awards/ Intercollegiate Biomathematics Alliance Distinguished Fellow.]

== Sample research publications ==

* K. Mahasa, L.G. de Pillis, R. Ouifki, A. Eladdadi, P. Maini, A.-R. Yoon, C.-O. Yun, ''[[doi:10.1038/s41598-019-57240-x|Mesenchymal Stem Cells Used as Carrier Cells of Oncolytic Adenovirus Results in Enhanced Oncolytic Virotherapy]],'' Nature Sci Rep 10, 425 (2020).
* L.G. de Pillis, with B. Shtylla, M. Gee, A. Do, S. Shabahang, and L. Eldevik, ''[https://www.frontiersin.org/article/10.3389/fphys.2019.01107 A Mathematical Model for DC Vaccine Treatment of Type I Diabetes]'', Frontiers in Physiology, Volume 10, 2019, article 1107.
* L.G. de Pillis, Erica J. Graham, Kaitlyn Hood, Yanping Ma, [[Ami Radunskaya]], and Julie Simons, ''Injury-Initiated Clot Formation Under Flow: A Mathematical Model with Warfarin Treatment,'' IMA Volumes in Mathematics and its Applications, Volume 158, 2015, pp.&nbsp;75–98.
* L.G. de Pillis, with E. Schwartz, O.O. Yang, W.G. Cumberland, ''Computational Model of HIV1 Escape from the Cytotoxic T Lymphocyte Response,'' Canadian Applied Mathematics Quarterly (CAMQ), Volume 21, Number 2, 2015, pp.&nbsp;261–279.
* L.G. de Pillis, A. Eladdadi, A.E. Radunskaya, ''Modeling Cancer-Immune Responses to Therapy'', Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics, Volume 41, Issue 5, October 2014, pp.&nbsp;461–478.
* L.G. de Pillis, with A.E. Radunskaya and C.L. Wiseman, [https://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/65/17/7950 ''A Validated Mathematical Model of Cell-Mediated Immune Response to Tumor Growth''], Cancer Research, Vol.61, No.17, pp.&nbsp;7950–7958, September 1, 2005.
